title: Analysis of the Microstructural Evolution of Lithium Metal during Electrodeposition and Subsequent Dissolution in “Anode-free” Solid-State Batteries using Electron-Backscatter Diffraction on Millimeter-Sized Cross-Sections
content: Lithium metal is a promising anode material, offering the potential for significantly higher energy densities in solid-state batteries [1]. However, its high reactivity poses considerable challenges during cell assembly. To further enhance energy density and simplify manufacturing, anode-free cells are investigated. In these cells, lithium is electrochemically plated during the initial charging step, eliminating the need to handle lithium foil during assembly [2]. Recently, a workflow has been established to characterize the microstructure of lithium in similar systems, which is crucial as its microstructure influences key performance parameters like stripping capacity [3-5]. Using this workflow, it may be possible to identify strategies to influence lithium microstructure, thereby improving battery performance. However, the current workflow has limited statistical validity as it only allows for the analysis of relatively small sample areas, restricting the significance of parameter studies.
